narrator.how: the narrator of an old book: evenly, with a light irony, not loud

fogg.how: an English gentleman: even, low, dry and precise, not one word too many, never raises his voice

passepartout.how: a young French manservant: lively, ringing, full of exclamations and a French “monsieur”

aouda.how: a young Indian woman: soft, quiet, with dignity

stuart.how: an English engineer at the club: weighty, with a smirk

cromarty.how: an old British general: brief, firm

guide.how: a young Parsee guide: quiet, quick, agitated

owner.how: an old Indian: stubborn, curt, not looking up

bunsby.how: an old pilot: hoarse, unhurried, a seaman's way

batulcar.how: the manager of a travelling troupe: loud, sing-song, like a barker at a fair

driver.how: an American engineer at the throttle: dashing, loud

mudge.how: a seasoned American: loud, cheerful, into the wind

speedy.how: a ruffian of a captain: roars, growls, guffaws

pastor.how: an old clergyman behind a door: calm, surprised
